docs.title: Welcome to AirDB
docs.text:
Decentralized, Local-First P2P Database Synchronization Engine over Bluetooth Low Energy

Zero Internet. Zero Central Servers. Automatic Peer Reconciliation. Cryptographic Provenance.

docs.title: What is AirDB?
docs.text: AirDB is an open-source, modular, local-first database replication engine designed for off-grid operations. When mobile devices running AirDB enter Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) proximity (~10–30 meters), they automatically discover each other, negotiate causal state differences, and stream database mutations directly device-to-device.

docs.title: Primary Use Cases
docs.text:
• Disaster Response & Emergency Camps: Coordinate survivor registries, triage status, and medical supplies in disaster zones where cellular towers and power grids are offline.
  • Off-Grid Mobile POS: Synchronize inventory, menu updates, and offline sales transactions across distributed cashier tablets at outdoor venues or remote markets.
  • Field Logistics & Conservation: Replicate wildlife observations, inspection checklists, and sensor logs between rangers in the field without satellite connectivity.

docs.title: Key Capabilities
docs.text:
• Dual-Role BLE Concurrency: Every device operates simultaneously as both a GATT Central (scanner) and GATT Peripheral (advertiser).
  • Sans-I/O Layered Design: Core causality logic, vector clocks, and wire codecs are 100% pure Kotlin and pure Swift standard libraries with zero socket or platform framework leaks.
  • Monotonic Hybrid Logical Clocks (HLC): Provides deterministic distributed causality and Last-Write-Wins (LWW) resolution without network time synchronization.
  • Zero-Trust Cryptographic Mesh:
  • Cluster Symmetric AEAD (RFC 8439): Payloads are encrypted with ChaCha20-Poly1305 using a 256-bit cluster key, 12-byte CSPRNG nonce, and full packet headers bound as Authenticated Additional Data (AAD).
  • Record-Level Digital Signatures (RFC 8032): Every mutation is signed by the originating author with Ed25519 (32-byte public key, 64-byte signature), enabling non-repudiation and tamper prevention across untrusted mesh relay hops.
  • Key Derivation (RFC 5869): HKDF-SHA256 for deterministic key material and subkey derivation.
  • Durable Local Persistence (BYOD): Built-in production SQLite storage engines (airdb-adapter-sqlite on Android/JVM and SqliteDbAdapter on Apple platforms) with Write-Ahead Logging (WAL), indexed HLC ranges, and atomic tombstone handling. Pluggable interface for Room, SQLDelight, GRDB, SwiftData, and CoreData.
  • Serialized In-Flight GATT Queue: Enforces single-flight operation ordering per link, eliminating native Bluetooth stack race conditions.
  • Automated Compression & Framing: Serializes compact binary packets, automatically compressing payloads (>256 B) via zlib Deflate and partitioning packets exceeding link MTU.
  • Deterministic Sans-I/O Simulator: Includes airdb-transport-sim and SimulatedTransport to test complete multi-node sync topologies in memory in milliseconds without hardware radios.

docs.title: Acknowledgements & Prior Art
docs.text:
AirDB's protocols, architecture, and design decisions were informed and inspired by foundational research and open-source projects across distributed systems, cryptography, and wireless mesh networks:

  • BitChat: For demonstrating the feasibility of ad-hoc mobile Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) mesh communication, dual-role GATT operation, and opportunistic store-and-forward relay mechanics in off-grid environments. AirDB is a clean-room implementation engineered specifically for structured database replication and causal consistency (CRDT/HLC), rather than ephemeral messaging.
  • Hybrid Logical Clocks (HLC): Based on the research paper "Logical Physical Clocks and Consistent Snapshots in Globally Distributed Databases" by Sandeep Kulkarni, Murat Demirbas, David Madeppa, Bharath Balasubramanian, and Sugumar Radhakrishnan (2014).
  • Vector Clocks & Distributed Ordering: Grounded in the foundational research of Leslie Lamport (1978), Colin Fidge (1988), and Friedemann Mattern (1988) on causal event ordering, partial order lattices, and state reconciliation.
  • The Local-First Software Movement: Inspired by the manifesto "Local-First Software: You Own Your Data, in spite of the Cloud" by Martin Kleppmann, Adam Wiggins, Peter van Hardenberg, and Mark McGranaghan (Ink & Switch, 2019).
  • SQLite Engine: Informed by D. Richard Hipp's architectural principles of crash resilience, Write-Ahead Logging (WAL), and zero-dependency embedded persistence.
  • RFC Cryptographic Standards: RFC 8439 (ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD), RFC 8032 (Ed25519 Digital Signatures), and RFC 5869 (HKDF-SHA256).

docs.title: AirDB Architecture Guide
docs.text: This document details the architectural principles, threading model, causal mathematics, persistence seam, and zero-trust cryptographic mesh that make AirDB robust in low-bandwidth, partition-heavy Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) environments.

docs.title: 1. Sans-I/O Architectural Discipline
docs.text:
A recurring failure mode in peer-to-peer mobile libraries is tightly coupling networking sockets or Bluetooth hardware delegates directly with state logic. This leads to queue-order deadlocks, difficult-to-reproduce race conditions, and tests that depend on physical wall-clock timeouts.

AirDB adopts a strict Sans-I/O architecture: * Protocol & Core logic are pure state transformations: They take an inbound event or byte array, compute transitions, and return outbound effects or state updates. * Platform boundary: Bluetooth managers, Android GATT callbacks, and hardware timers exist exclusively in airdb-transport-ble and CoreBluetoothTransport. * Instant simulation: Because the core engine communicates via AirDbTransport interfaces, SimulatedTransport allows testing complex multi-node network topologies (with simulated packet drops, reordering, and partitions) completely in memory in milliseconds.

docs.title: The Android Single-Flight GATT Invariant
docs.text:
The native Android Bluetooth stack (BlueDroid/Fluoride) is asynchronous and single-flight per connection. If an application invokes writeCharacteristic or notifyCharacteristicChanged while an existing operation is pending, the Android stack either rejects the call immediately or drops the packet silently.

AirDB solves this with GattOperationQueue: * State per link: Every active physical link has an isolated FIFO operation queue with an inFlight boolean flag. * Trigger on callback: The next operation in queue is dispatched ONLY when the driver invokes onCharacteristicWrite (Central) or onNotificationSent (Server). * Backpressure bounds: Queues enforce a strict capacity limit (default 256 operations or 1 MiB) with exponential backoff on transient stack errors.

docs.title: Swift Actor Model on Apple Platforms
docs.text: On Apple platforms, AirDbKit implements the core engine as a Swift actor: * Data Race Freedom: Compile-time enforcement of isolated mutable state across threads. * Non-Blocking Delegates: Asynchronous CoreBluetooth delegate callbacks forward frames into structured Swift tasks without blocking radio threads. * Zero Third-Party Dependencies: Relies 100% on Apple standard frameworks (CryptoKit, Compression, CoreBluetooth, and native libsqlite3).

docs.title: Hybrid Logical Clocks (HLC)
docs.text:
In off-grid disaster environments or mobile POS setups, physical system clocks can drift by minutes or hours due to lack of network time synchronization (NTP).

AirDB uses Hybrid Logical Clocks (HLC) combining physical time, an incrementing counter, and a node tie-breaker:

T = (pt, lc, nodeId)

Where: * \(pt \in \mathbb{N}_0\): Physical time (epoch milliseconds). * \(lc \in \mathbb{N}_0\): Monotonic logical counter for events sharing the same physical millisecond. * \(nodeId \in \Sigma^+\): Globally unique node identifier ensuring total ordering.

docs.title: Total Order Relation (\(<_{HLC}\))
docs.text:
For any two timestamps \(T_1 = (pt_1, lc_1, node_1)\) and \(T_2 = (pt_2, lc_2, node_2)\), the strict total order \(<_{HLC}\) is defined lexicographically:

T_1 <_{HLC} T_2 \iff \begin{cases}
pt_1 < pt_2 \\
pt_1 = pt_2 \land lc_1 < lc_2 \\
pt_1 = pt_2 \land lc_1 = lc_2 \land node_1 <_{lex} node_2
\end{cases}

This relation forms a strict total order: irreflexive, asymmetric, transitive, and connex. Every pair of timestamps is deterministically comparable across all distributed replicas.

docs.title: Rule 1: Local Mutation
docs.text:
When generating a new timestamp on node \(j\):

pt' = \max(latest.pt, \text{now}())

lc' = \begin{cases}
latest.lc + 1 & \text{if } pt' = latest.pt \\
0 & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}

docs.title: Rule 2: Remote Message Ingestion
docs.text:
When node \(j\) observes remote timestamp \(T_{remote} = (pt_{rem}, lc_{rem}, node_{rem})\):

pt' = \max(\max(latest.pt, pt_{rem}), \text{now}())

lc' = \begin{cases}
\max(latest.lc, lc_{rem}) + 1 & \text{if } pt' = latest.pt = pt_{rem} \\
latest.lc + 1 & \text{if } pt' = latest.pt \\
lc_{rem} + 1 & \text{if } pt' = pt_{rem} \\
0 & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}

docs.title: 4. Vector Clock State Tracking & Delta Reconciliation
Formal Definition of Vector Clock
docs.text:
A Vector Clock \(V\) on a node is a partial function mapping originating node identifiers to their highest known causal HLC timestamp:

V : \text{NodeId} \to \text{HLC}

docs.title: Causal Dominance & Partial Order
docs.text:
Given two vector clocks \(V_A\) and \(V_B\):

V_A \le V_B \iff \forall k \in \text{dom}(V_A): V_A[k] \le_{HLC} V_B[k]

V_A < V_B \iff (V_A \le V_B) \land (V_A \ne V_B)

If neither \(V_A \le V_B\) nor \(V_B \le V_A\), the states are causally concurrent:

V_A \parallel V_B \iff \neg(V_A \le V_B) \land \neg(V_B \le V_A)

docs.title: Exact Delta Reconciliation Set
docs.text:
When node \(B\) reconciles with node \(A\) presenting knowledge vector \(V_A\), the minimal missing delta batch \(\Delta(B \to A)\) is computed as:

\Delta(B \to A) = \left\{ r \in \text{Records}_B \mid r.hlc >_{HLC} V_A[r.nodeId] \right\}

Where \(V_A[r.nodeId] = -\infty\) if \(r.nodeId \notin \text{dom}(V_A)\).

This invariant guarantees that: 1. Re-connecting nodes transmit only novel mutations created during partition intervals. 2. Bandwidth consumption over BLE is strictly bounded to missing records \(\mathcal{O}(|\Delta|)\) rather than total database size \(\mathcal{O}(|\text{DB}|)\).

docs.title: Conflict Resolution: Last-Write-Wins (LWW)
docs.text:
For any record key \(K\) subject to concurrent mutations \(M_A\) and \(M_B\):

\text{Winner}(K) = \begin{cases}
M_A & \text{if } M_A.hlc >_{HLC} M_B.hlc \\
M_B & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}

docs.title: Convergence Theorem
docs.text:
Under epidemic pairwise gossip across any connected graph component \(G = (V, E)\), the database state \(S_i(t)\) of every node \(i\) monotonically converges:

\lim_{t \to \infty} S_i(t) = S_j(t) = \bigcup_{k \in \text{Keys}} \max_{<_{HLC}} \left( \text{Mutations}(k) \right)

All replicas independently reach 100% causal identity without central coordination or distributed consensus rounds.

docs.title: 5. Durable SQLite Persistence Seam
docs.text: AirDB provides production-ready, durable storage engines across all platforms: * Android / JVM: SqliteAirDbAdapter in :airdb-adapter-sqlite. * Apple Platforms: SqliteDbAdapter in AirDbKit utilizing native libsqlite3.

docs.title: Schema Architecture & Change Tracking
docs.text:
The underlying storage maintains an append-only, indexed changelog table alongside domain tables:

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS _airdb_changes (
    collection TEXT NOT NULL,
    id TEXT NOT NULL,
    mutation_type INTEGER NOT NULL,
    payload BLOB,
    hlc_timestamp TEXT NOT NULL,
    author_public_key BLOB,
    signature BLOB,
    created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (collection, id)
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_airdb_changes_hlc
ON _airdb_changes(hlc_timestamp ASC);

docs.title: Durability & ACID Guarantees
docs.text:
1. Write-Ahead Logging (WAL): All adapters enable PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL and PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL, permitting non-blocking concurrent readers during write transactions.
  2. Atomic Batch Application: Inbound delta batches are applied inside an immediate transaction (BEGIN IMMEDIATE ... COMMIT). If verification fails or disk write aborts, the transaction rolls back cleanly.
  3. Anti-Resurrection Tombstone Lifecycle: Soft-deleted entities retain an entry with mutation_type = 2 (DELETE) and the tombstone HLC timestamp. Any inbound mutation with an older timestamp is discarded, preventing obsolete sync passes from resurrecting deleted records.

docs.title: 6. Zero-Trust Cryptographic Mesh & Provenance
docs.text:
In off-grid, multi-hop mesh deployments (such as disaster survivor coordination or remote mobile POS networks), packets pass through intermediate relay devices that may be untrusted, misconfigured, or adversarial. AirDB implements a two-tier Zero-Trust Cryptographic Mesh.

+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Layer 1: Cluster-Level Symmetric AEAD (RFC 8439 ChaCha20-Poly1305)             |
| Encrypts over-the-air payload, binds packet header as AAD, authenticates link  |
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Layer 2: Record-Level Asymmetric Signatures (RFC 8032 Ed25519)                 |
| Cryptographically binds each mutation to author public key, prevents forgery   |
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| Layer 3: Key Derivation & Session Materials (RFC 5869 HKDF-SHA256)             |
| Deterministically derives cluster and session keys from shared pre-shared keys |
+---------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

docs.title: Layer 1: Cluster-Level Symmetric AEAD (ChaCha20-Poly1305)
docs.text:
To prevent eavesdropping and unauthorized packet injection into a local operational cluster: 1. AEAD Cipher: ChaCha20-Poly1305 (RFC 8439) with a 256-bit symmetric clusterKey. 2. Header Authentication Binding (AAD): The entire 23-byte (or 31-byte) wire header—including magic, version, type, flags, timestamp, payloadLength, senderId, and optional recipientId—is passed as Authenticated Additional Data (\(AAD\)). 3. Nonce Construction: A fresh 12-byte CSPRNG nonce is generated for every encrypted transmission. 4. Wire Representation:

\text{WirePayload} = \text{Nonce}_{12\text{B}} \parallel \text{Ciphertext}_{N\text{B}} \parallel \text{Tag}_{16\text{B}}

Any modification to the header flags, timestamp, or ciphertext causes Poly1305 verification failure, resulting in silent drop before payload parsing.

docs.title: Layer 2: Record-Level Asymmetric Signatures (Ed25519)
docs.text: Cluster encryption protects over-the-air frames between immediate peers. However, in a multi-hop mesh network, intermediate relay nodes decrypt and forward packets. To ensure malicious or compromised relays cannot forge, alter, or backdate database records, every mutation is digitally signed by the original author.

docs.title: Canonical Signing Tuple
docs.text:
For a record \(R\), the canonical byte representation for signing is:

M(R) = \text{collection} \parallel \text{id} \parallel \text{type} \parallel \text{hlcTimestamp} \parallel \text{payload}

docs.title: Signature Generation
docs.text:
The originating node signs \(M(R)\) using its private Ed25519 key:

\sigma = \text{Ed25519Sign}(\text{PrivateKey}_{author}, M(R))

The resulting 32-byte author public key and 64-byte signature \(\sigma\) are attached directly to the ChangeRecord.

docs.title: Zero-Trust Verification Rule
docs.text:
When a receiving node processes incoming records with enforceSignatures = true:

\text{Valid}(R) = \begin{cases}
1 & \text{if } \text{Ed25519Verify}(\text{PublicKey}_{author}, M(R), \sigma) = \text{true} \\
0 & \text{otherwise}
\end{cases}

If \(\text{Valid}(R) = 0\), the mutation is dropped immediately. It is never applied to the local database adapter nor forwarded to downstream gossip peers.

docs.title: AirDbKit
docs.text:
Swift implementation of the AirDB peer-to-peer database replication engine for Apple platforms (iOS, macOS, watchOS, and visionOS).

AirDbKit provides decentralized, local-first synchronization over Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE). It has zero dependency on central servers, cellular internet, or cloud infrastructure, making it suitable for disaster response, emergency medical triage, remote logistics, and mobile point-of-sale environments.

AirDbKit maintains 100% on-wire binary compatibility with AirDB for Android and Kotlin/JVM.

docs.title: Architectural Principles
docs.text:
1. Sans-I/O Layering: Pure causal replication and wire serialization decoupled from I/O mechanisms.
  2. Actor Concurrency: Built with Swift structured concurrency (actor, async/await, Sendable) ensuring compile-time data race freedom.
  3. Zero Third-Party Dependencies: Built exclusively on Apple standard frameworks (CryptoKit, Compression, CoreBluetooth, and libsqlite3). No external CocoaPods or SPM package dependencies.
  4. Zero-Trust Cryptographic Mesh:
  5. Cluster-level AEAD symmetric encryption via ChaChaPolyCipher (RFC 8439 ChaCha20-Poly1305) with packet header authentication.
  6. Record-level digital signatures via Ed25519Signer (RFC 8032) for cryptographic provenance and tamper detection across untrusted relay nodes.
  7. Key derivation via HkdfSha256 (RFC 5869).
  8. Durable Persistence Engine: Built-in SqliteDbAdapter with Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) and atomic transactions.
  9. Resilient BLE Transport: Dual-role CoreBluetoothTransport (Central + Peripheral) with MTU fragmentation, 30-second TTL assembly, and backpressure flow control.

docs.title: Swift Package Manager (SPM)
docs.text:
In Xcode: 1. Select File > Add Package Dependencies... 2. Enter the repository URL: 

https://github.com/untacorp/airdb.git
3. Set dependency rule to branch main or specific version tag. 4. Add AirDbKit to your application target.

Or add it directly to your Package.swift:

dependencies: [
    .package(url: "https://github.com/untacorp/airdb.git", branch: "main")
]

docs.text: Platform Minimum Deployment Target iOS 15.0+ macOS 12.0+ watchOS 8.0+ tvOS 15.0+ Swift 5.9+

docs.title: 1. Configure Info.plist for Bluetooth
docs.text:
To enable Bluetooth peripheral and central roles on iOS, declare the following privacy keys in your application Info.plist:

<key>NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription</key>
<string>AirDB synchronizes local records with nearby responders over Bluetooth Low Energy.</string>
<key>NSBluetoothPeripheralUsageDescription</key>
<string>AirDB advertises local database changes to nearby devices.</string>
<key>UIBackgroundModes</key>
<array>
    <string>bluetooth-central</string>
    <string>bluetooth-peripheral</string>
</array>

docs.title: 2. Initialize AirDB Engine with Security and Durable SQLite
docs.text:
import AirDbKit
import Foundation

// 1. Initialize durable native SQLite persistence
let dbPath = FileManager.default.urls(for: .documentDirectory, in: .userDomainMask)[0]
    .appendingPathComponent("airdb.db").path
let adapter = try SqliteDbAdapter(databasePath: dbPath)

// 2. Derive cluster encryption key and node signing key pair
let clusterKey = try HkdfSha256.deriveKey(
    secret: "emergency-cluster-shared-secret".data(using: .utf8)!,
    salt: "airdb-mesh-v1".data(using: .utf8)!,
    info: "cluster-aead-key".data(using: .utf8)!
)
let authorKeyPair = try Ed25519Signer.generateKeyPair()

// 3. Initialize CoreBluetooth transport
let transport = CoreBluetoothTransport()

// 4. Create the AirDB Engine with cryptographic provenance enforcement
let engine = AirDbEngine(
    nodeName: "posko-merapi-ios-01",
    adapter: adapter,
    transport: transport,
    clusterKey: clusterKey,
    authorKeyPair: authorKeyPair,
    enforceSignatures: true
)

// 5. Listen for synchronization updates from nearby peers
engine.addSyncListener { peerId, changeCount in
    print("Synchronized \(changeCount) verified records from peer: \(peerId)")
}

// 6. Start radio operations
engine.start()

docs.title: 3. Record Mutations
docs.text:
Save records locally using saveRecord. Every mutation is stamped with an authoritative Hybrid Logical Clock (HLC) timestamp, signed with the local authorKeyPair, and propagated to discovered peers:

let payload = """
{
    "patientId": "P-9842",
    "name": "Siti Rahma",
    "triage": "YELLOW",
    "pulse": 88
}
""".data(using: .utf8)!

let record = try await engine.saveRecord(
    collection: "triage_assessments",
    id: "P-9842",
    type: .insert,
    payload: payload
)

print("Saved change record: \(record.id) with HLC: \(record.hlcTimestamp)")
print("Author public key: \(record.authorPublicKey?.count ?? 0) bytes")

docs.title: Wire Protocol Compatibility
docs.text:
AirDbKit adheres strictly to docs/PROTOCOL_SPEC.md:

  • GATT Service UUID: 41697244-4200-0000-8000-00805F9B34FB
  • GATT Characteristic UUID: 41697244-4201-0000-8000-00805F9B34FB
  • Magic Bytes: 0x41 0x44 ("AD")
  • Network Byte Order: Big-Endian multi-byte integers
  • AEAD Encryption: ChaCha20-Poly1305 (FLAG_ENCRYPTED = 0x04) with 12-byte nonce, 16-byte Poly1305 authentication tag, and header bound as AAD.
  • Cryptographic Provenance: Ed25519 digital signatures (FLAG_RECORD_SIGNED = 0x80) on delta batches with 32-byte public key and 64-byte signature.
  • Deflate Compression: Apple Compression framework zlib integration for payloads > 256 bytes (FLAG_COMPRESSED = 0x01).
  • Fragmentation: 13-byte fragment envelope with sliding 30-second TTL reassembly buffer.

  • BleConfig defining UUIDs, 517-byte target MTU, and transmission policies.
  • Samples:
  • airdb-sim-demo: Runnable disaster relief emergency posko sync scenario demonstrating causal data convergence.

docs.title: AirDB Coding & Engineering Standards
docs.text: These standards ensure that AirDB maintains high architectural integrity, safety, security, and readability as an enterprise-grade open-source project.

docs.title: 1. Concurrency & Thread-Safety
docs.text:
1. State Isolation:
  2. Internal JVM collections must be thread-safe (ConcurrentHashMap, CopyOnWriteArrayList, or atomic primitives).
  3. Any mutable critical sections across multiple fields must be protected by explicit locks (synchronized(lock) { ... }).
  4. On Apple platforms, mutable state must be encapsulated within Swift actor types or protected by lock closures (NSLock.withScopedLock).
  5. Non-Blocking Delegates:
  6. Never call Thread.sleep() or blocking I/O inside transport callbacks or event listeners.
  7. Use Kotlin Coroutines (CoroutineScope, launch, delay) with appropriate dispatchers (Dispatchers.Default for CPU/state machine, Dispatchers.IO for disk adapters).
  8. In Swift, delegate methods must dispatch work asynchronously to actor tasks without blocking CoreBluetooth delegate queues.

docs.title: 2. API Design & Seams
docs.text:
1. Clean Seams:
  2. High-level business logic must never know about Android Bluetooth classes (BluetoothGatt, BluetoothDevice) or Apple CoreBluetooth classes (CBPeripheral, CBCentralManager).
  3. All I/O must enter and leave through AirDbTransport and AirDbAdapter interfaces.
  4. KDoc & SwiftDoc Coverage:
  5. Every public interface, class, actor, and method MUST have comprehensive documentation describing:
    • Purpose and invariants
    • Thread-safety guarantees
    • Parameter descriptions
    • Return values and error conditions

docs.title: 3. Cryptographic Invariants & Zero-Trust Mesh
docs.text:
1. Authenticated Wire Framing:
  2. Every encrypted packet must bind the complete wire header into the AEAD cipher as Authenticated Additional Data (\(AAD\)).
  3. Never decrypt payloads without validating the Poly1305 MAC tag.
  4. Record Signing Hygiene:
  5. The canonical signing buffer must deterministically serialize collection, ID, mutation type, HLC timestamp, and payload bytes in Big-Endian order.
  6. Inbound records must be verified against author public keys prior to calling applyChanges.
  7. Key Derivation Standards:
  8. Use RFC 5869 HKDF-SHA256 with distinct domain separation strings (info tags) for symmetric cluster keys.

docs.title: 4. Dependencies & Platform Purity
docs.text:
1. Sans-I/O Core:
  2. airdb-core, airdb-protocol, airdb-crypto, and airdb-adapter-api must remain 100% pure Kotlin with zero dependencies on the Android SDK (android.*).
  3. Zero Third-Party SPM Dependencies:
  4. AirDbKit must strictly rely on native Apple standard frameworks (CryptoKit, Compression, CoreBluetooth, and libsqlite3). No external SPM packages.

docs.title: 5. Zero-Emoji Policy
docs.text:
1. Strictly zero emojis across all code, tests, comments, docstrings, commit messages, PR descriptions, and markdown documentation.
  2. Automated scanners reject any pull requests containing emoji characters.

docs.title: 6. Testing Rules
docs.text:
1. Deterministic Tests:
  2. No Thread.sleep in tests. Use coroutine test dispatchers (runTest, advanceTimeBy, StandardTestDispatcher) or CountDownLatch with explicit timeouts.
  3. Property & Fuzz Testing:
  4. Binary serialization and reassembly logic must be tested with edge cases: 0-byte arrays, maximum integer limits, and out-of-order chunk arrival.
  5. Cryptographic Coverage:
  6. All AEAD ciphers and digital signature implementations must be verified against known RFC test vectors or round-trip tampering assertions.

docs.title: Contributing to AirDB
docs.text:
Thank you for your interest in contributing to AirDB. This project is a local-first, peer-to-peer, offline database engine designed for resilient low-bandwidth Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) environments.

To maintain engineering excellence across both Kotlin and Swift codebases, please adhere to the following standards.

docs.title: 1. Zero-Emoji Policy
docs.text: This repository strictly enforces a Zero-Emoji Policy. - Do not use emoji characters anywhere: in source code, inline comments, commit messages, PR descriptions, or documentation files. - Automated CI linters will reject any pull requests containing emoji characters.

docs.title: 2. Commit Message Standardization
docs.text: AirDB strictly follows the Conventional Commits v1.0.0 specification.

docs.title: Commit Format
docs.text:
<type>(<scope>): <short summary in imperative mood>

[optional body explaining context, rationale, and technical decisions]

[optional footer for issue tracking or breaking changes]

docs.title: Allowed Types
docs.text:
• feat: Adds a new user-facing or platform feature.
  • fix: Fixes a bug or handles an edge case in reconciliation or transport.
  • perf: Improves runtime throughput, latency, or memory allocations without API changes.
  • docs: Updates architecture documents, protocol specifications, or guides.
  • test: Adds or fixes unit tests, integration tests, or simulation scenarios.
  • refactor: Changes code structure without changing functional behavior.
  • ci: Modifies GitHub Actions workflows or build automation scripts.
  • chore: Updates dependencies, Gradle/SPM metadata, or repository tooling.

docs.title: Standard Scopes
docs.text:
• core: State store, CRDT engine, HLC (Hybrid Logical Clock), Vector Clock.
  • protocol: Binary wire format, CBOR serialization, AssemblyBuffer, Delta framing.
  • ble-android: AndroidBleTransport, AndroidBlePermissions, GattOperationQueue.
  • ble-ios: Apple AirDbKit, CoreBluetooth driver (AppleBleTransport).
  • sim: Virtual BLE simulation transport (SimulatedBleTransport).
  • adapter: Adapter API, SQLite/Room/CoreData integration contracts.
  • crypto: Cryptographic mesh, ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD, Ed25519 signatures, HKDF.
  • arch: Architectural definitions, formal mathematical proofs.
  • ci: GitHub Actions workflows and build pipelines.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
Good: - feat(ble-android): implement AndroidBleTransport driver with single-flight GATT queue - fix(core): resolve HLC comparison bug when counter values exceed 9 - docs(arch): formalize monotonic convergence proof under partial order - test(ble-android): add AndroidBlePermissions test matrix for API 31 and legacy

Bad: - update ble stuff (missing type, scope, and context) - feat: fixed a bug and added tests (mixed concerns, imperative mood violated) - fix: fixed bug with emojis (violates Zero-Emoji Policy)

docs.title: 3. Branch Naming Conventions
docs.text:
Branch names should reflect the work being conducted: - feat/<short-description>: New capabilities or transport drivers. - fix/<short-description>: Bug fixes and edge case remediation. - docs/<short-description>: Documentation improvements. - refactor/<short-description>: Non-functional structural enhancements.

Example: feat/android-ble-driver, fix/hlc-string-order.

docs.title: 4. Code Quality and Testing Standards
docs.text:
Before submitting changes or pushing commits: 1. Ensure all JVM unit tests pass: 

./gradlew test
2. Verify end-to-end simulation: 
./gradlew :airdb-samples:airdb-sim-demo:run
3. If modifying Apple Swift packages (AirDbKit): 
cd AirDbKit && swift test
4. Verify zero compiler warnings. 5. All new source files must include the standard Apache-2.0 license header.

docs.title: 5. Architecture Principles
docs.text:
• Sans-I/O Engine: Keep airdb-core and airdb-protocol completely free of OS-specific I/O or platform libraries.
  • Backpressure Discipline: Bluetooth LE operations on Android and iOS must be strictly single-flight per connection. Never call writeCharacteristic or requestMtu concurrently before receiving the corresponding callback.
  • Monotonic Causality: State mutations must remain causally monotonic. State reconciliations must be idempotent, commutative, and associative (\(A \sqcup B = B \sqcup A\)).

docs.title: 1. How does AirDB handle physical clock skew if a device's battery dies or clock resets to 1970?
docs.text: AirDB uses Hybrid Logical Clocks (HLC). When a device with a reset or lagging clock receives incoming mutations from peers, its local HLC immediately ratchets forward to match the highest observed physical time and advances the logical counter. Local writes will always be monotonically newer than prior observed events, ensuring data consistency even without NTP access.

docs.title: 2. What happens if a record is deleted on Node A, while an old offline Node B updates the same record?
docs.text: AirDB enforces tombstone causality: - When an entity is deleted, a tombstone record with MutationType.DELETE is assigned an HLC timestamp. - If an update from Node B arrives with an HLC timestamp older than the tombstone's timestamp, the update is rejected and the record remains deleted. - If Node B (or any node) explicitly writes a brand-new update after learning about the deletion (giving it a newer HLC timestamp), the record is cleanly recreated.

docs.title: 3. How does AirDB prevent Bluetooth battery drain?
docs.text: Continuous BLE scanning consumes significant power. AirDB is designed to integrate with power managers: - Central scanning can be duty-cycled (e.g. active for 2 seconds, idle for 8 seconds) when devices are stationary. - Advertising payloads use minimal 31-byte legacy packets (Service UUID + NodeID) to minimize radio airtime. - Payloads >256 bytes are automatically compressed with zlib Deflate, reducing packet transmission time by 50–70%.

docs.title: 4. Can AirDB sync large binary files (e.g. photos or database dumps)?
docs.text: BLE throughput is physically bounded (~20 KB/s to 80 KB/s). AirDB is optimized for structured delta changes, JSON, Protobuf, and transactional records. For multi-megabyte photo or video attachments, the recommended pattern is: 1. Replicate metadata, checksums, and references via AirDB over BLE. 2. Trigger an out-of-band P2P high-speed transfer (such as Wi-Fi Aware / Wi-Fi Direct) for the heavy binary blob when needed.

docs.title: 5. Why use the built-in SQLite adapter vs a custom Room adapter?
docs.text: AirDB provides SqliteAirDbAdapter (airdb-adapter-sqlite) and SqliteDbAdapter (AirDbKit) as turnkey, production-ready storage engines with Write-Ahead Logging (WAL) and indexed HLC ranges. However, by defining AirDbAdapter, AirDB remains completely agnostic of your application's schema, ORM, and platform. You can plug in Room, SQLCipher, Realm, CoreData, GRDB, or simple in-memory key-value maps.

docs.title: 6. How does AirDB secure communication against eavesdropping and rogue nodes?
docs.text: AirDB incorporates RFC 8439 ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD symmetric encryption at the cluster layer. When a clusterKey is configured: - All packet payloads are encrypted on the wire. - The entire wire header (including packet types, timestamp, flags, sender ID, and recipient ID) is bound into the Poly1305 MAC as Authenticated Additional Data (\(AAD\)). - Any unauthorized injection or wire bit-flip fails authentication and is silently dropped prior to parsing.

docs.title: 7. Can an intermediate relay node alter records during multi-hop gossip synchronization?
docs.text: No. AirDB employs RFC 8032 Ed25519 digital signatures on every mutation record: - The originating author node cryptographically signs the record's collection, ID, mutation type, HLC timestamp, and payload with its private key. - Relaying nodes forward the signed record verbatim. - Receiving nodes verify the Ed25519 signature against the author's public key before applying changes. If an intermediate node modifies the payload or manipulates the HLC timestamp, the signature check fails and the mutation is rejected.

docs.title: 8. Does AirDbKit require third-party dependencies on iOS or macOS?
docs.text: Zero. AirDbKit is implemented entirely with Apple standard library frameworks: - Cryptography: CryptoKit (ChaChaPoly, Curve25519.Signing, HKDF) - Persistence: libsqlite3 (native SQLite C-bindings) - Compression: Apple Compression framework (zlib Deflate) - Transport: CoreBluetooth This ensures zero supply-chain risk and zero dependency management overhead.

docs.title: Getting Started with AirDB
docs.text: This guide walks you through integrating AirDB into an Android application, Kotlin JVM service, or Apple application (iOS/macOS) to enable peer-to-peer database synchronization over Bluetooth Low Energy with zero-trust cryptographic guarantees.

docs.title: Android & Kotlin JVM (build.gradle.kts)
docs.text:
dependencies {
    implementation("io.airdb:airdb-core:0.2.0")
    implementation("io.airdb:airdb-protocol:0.2.0")
    implementation("io.airdb:airdb-crypto:0.2.0")
    implementation("io.airdb:airdb-adapter-sqlite:0.2.0")
    implementation("io.airdb:airdb-transport-ble:0.2.0")
}

docs.title: Apple Platforms (Package.swift or Xcode SPM)
docs.text:
dependencies: [
    .package(url: "https://github.com/untacorp/airdb.git", branch: "main")
]

docs.title: 2. Setting Up Durable SQLite Persistence
docs.text: AirDB provides out-of-the-box persistent storage via SQLite WAL mode, eliminating the need to write boilerplate database adapters.

docs.title: Kotlin / Android:
docs.text:
import io.airdb.adapter.sqlite.SqliteAirDbAdapter

val dbFile = context.getDatabasePath("airdb_posko.db")
val adapter = SqliteAirDbAdapter(dbPath = dbFile.absolutePath)

docs.title: Apple Platforms / Swift:
docs.text:
import AirDbKit

let dbPath = FileManager.default.urls(for: .documentDirectory, in: .userDomainMask)[0]
    .appendingPathComponent("airdb_posko.db").path
let adapter = try SqliteDbAdapter(databasePath: dbPath)

(Note: If your application already uses Room, SQLDelight, GRDB, or CoreData, you can implement the clean AirDbAdapter interface directly).

docs.title: 3. Configuring Cryptographic Keys (Zero-Trust Mesh)
docs.text: AirDB protects data in flight using ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD and verifies record authenticity using Ed25519 digital signatures.

docs.title: Kotlin / Android:
docs.text:
import io.airdb.crypto.Ed25519Signer
import io.airdb.crypto.HkdfSha256

// 1. Derive 256-bit symmetric AEAD cluster key from pre-shared secret
val clusterKey = HkdfSha256.deriveKey(
    ikm = "disaster-relief-cluster-secret".toByteArray(Charsets.UTF_8),
    salt = "airdb-mesh-v1".toByteArray(Charsets.UTF_8),
    info = "cluster-aead-key".toByteArray(Charsets.UTF_8)
)

// 2. Generate or load local device's Ed25519 signing key pair
val authorKeyPair = Ed25519Signer.generateKeyPair()

docs.title: Apple Platforms / Swift:
docs.text:
import AirDbKit

let clusterKey = try HkdfSha256.deriveKey(
    secret: "disaster-relief-cluster-secret".data(using: .utf8)!,
    salt: "airdb-mesh-v1".data(using: .utf8)!,
    info: "cluster-aead-key".data(using: .utf8)!
)

let authorKeyPair = try Ed25519Signer.generateKeyPair()

docs.title: Android / Kotlin:
docs.text:
import io.airdb.core.engine.AirDbEngine
import io.airdb.transport.ble.AndroidBleTransport

val transport = AndroidBleTransport(context)

val engine = AirDbEngine(
    nodeName = "posko-merapi-1",
    adapter = adapter,
    transport = transport,
    clusterKey = clusterKey,
    authorKeyPair = authorKeyPair,
    enforceSignatures = true
)

// Register listener for sync progress
engine.addSyncListener { peerId, changeCount ->
    Log.i("AirDB", "Applied $changeCount verified mutations from peer: $peerId")
}

// Start discovery and synchronization
engine.start()

docs.title: Apple / Swift:
docs.text:
import AirDbKit

let transport = CoreBluetoothTransport()

let engine = AirDbEngine(
    nodeName: "posko-merapi-ios-01",
    adapter = adapter,
    transport = transport,
    clusterKey = clusterKey,
    authorKeyPair = authorKeyPair,
    enforceSignatures = true
)

engine.addSyncListener { peerId, changeCount in
    print("Applied \(changeCount) verified mutations from peer: \(peerId)")
}

engine.start()

docs.title: 5. Saving and Propagating Mutations
docs.text: When your application creates, updates, or deletes records, invoke engine.saveRecord():

docs.title: Android / Kotlin:
docs.text:
import io.airdb.adapter.MutationType

val triageJson = """{"patientId": "P-101", "name": "Budi", "triage": "YELLOW"}"""

engine.saveRecord(
    collection = "triage_assessments",
    id = "P-101",
    type = MutationType.INSERT,
    payload = triageJson.toByteArray(Charsets.UTF_8)
)

docs.title: Apple / Swift:
docs.text:
let triageJson = """{"patientId": "P-101", "name": "Budi", "triage": "YELLOW"}""".data(using: .utf8)!

let record = try await engine.saveRecord(
    collection: "triage_assessments",
    id: "P-101",
    type: .insert,
    payload: triageJson
)

The mutation is automatically stamped with a monotonic HLC timestamp, signed with the local private key, written to persistent storage, and synchronized to all discovered peers within BLE proximity.

docs.title: AirDB Wire Protocol Specification (v1)
docs.text: This specification defines the on-wire binary packet formats, framing, AEAD encryption envelope, fragmentation, and handshake sequence for AirDB over Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE).

docs.title: 1. Network Byte Order
docs.text: All multi-byte numeric values (Short, Int, Long) are encoded in Network Byte Order (Big-Endian).

docs.title: Header Fields:
docs.text:
• Magic (2 bytes): Fixed ASCII bytes 0x41 0x44 ("AD" for AirDB). Rejects stray packets from unrelated BLE networks.
  • Version (1 byte): Protocol version. Currently 0x01.
  • Type (1 byte): Packet type code:
  • 0x01: HANDSHAKE
  • 0x02: HANDSHAKE_ACK
  • 0x03: RECONCILE_REQ
  • 0x04: RECONCILE_RESP
  • 0x05: DELTA_BATCH
  • 0x06: DELTA_ACK
  • 0x0F: FRAGMENT
  • Flags (1 byte): Bitmask indicating payload transformations:
  • Bit 0 (0x01): FLAG_COMPRESSED (Payload is zlib Deflate compressed).
  • Bit 1 (0x02): FLAG_HAS_RECIPIENT (8-byte Recipient ID is present in header).
  • Bit 2 (0x04): FLAG_ENCRYPTED (Payload is encrypted with ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD).
  • Timestamp (8 bytes): Epoch millisecond timestamp of packet creation.
  • Payload Length (2 bytes): Unsigned 16-bit integer defining the byte length of the trailing payload (or ciphertext payload).
  • Sender ID (8 bytes): 64-bit identifier of the transmitting node.
  • Recipient ID (8 bytes, optional): 64-bit identifier of the target node (present only if FLAG_HAS_RECIPIENT is set).

docs.title: 3. Cryptographic Envelope (FLAG_ENCRYPTED = 0x04)
docs.text:
When FLAG_ENCRYPTED is asserted in the packet header, the payload region consists of an RFC 8439 ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD ciphertext:

Encrypted Payload Wire Layout:
+--------------------+-------------------------------------------+--------------------+
| Nonce (12 bytes)   | Ciphertext (N bytes)                      | Poly1305 Tag (16B) |
+--------------------+-------------------------------------------+--------------------+

docs.title: Authenticated Additional Data (AAD) Binding:
docs.text: To prevent header tampering, type-confusion attacks, sender spoofing, and replay splicing: 1. The entire wire header (23 bytes without recipient, 31 bytes with recipient) is passed directly as the \(AAD\) input to the Poly1305 MAC calculator. 2. The decryption routine recalculates the Poly1305 MAC over the received wire header and ciphertext. 3. If any header field (such as timestamp, senderId, type, or flags) was altered in transit, the MAC fails verification and the packet is immediately discarded without parsing.

docs.title: 4. Fragmentation Format (FragmentHeader)
docs.text:
When a serialized packet exceeds link MTU boundaries (typically > 460 bytes), it is partitioned into fragments:

Fragment Envelope (13 bytes):
+--------------------+------------------+------------------+--------------------+-------------------+
| Fragment ID (8B)   | Index (2B BE)    | Total (2B BE)    | Original Type (1B) | Chunk Data        |
+--------------------+------------------+------------------+--------------------+-------------------+
  • Fragment ID (8 bytes): Randomly generated identifier grouping chunks belonging to the same packet.
  • Index (2 bytes): 0-based sequence index.
  • Total (2 bytes): Total number of fragments in this assembly.
  • Original Type (1 byte): Packet type of the original reassembled packet.
  • Chunk Data: Sub-slice of the original packet's binary wire data.
  • Assembly Buffer Lifecycle: Slices are buffered in an AssemblyBuffer with a 30-second sliding TTL. Expired or incomplete frames are purged automatically to prevent memory leaks.

docs.title: Mutation Type Byte:
docs.text:
• Bits 0–6:
  • 0x00: INSERT
  • 0x01: UPDATE
  • 0x02: DELETE
  • Bit 7 (0x80): FLAG_RECORD_SIGNED
  • When 0: Unsigned record (no trailing public key or signature).
  • When 1: Signed record. Trailing 32 bytes contain the author's Ed25519 public key, followed by 64 bytes containing the Ed25519 digital signature.

docs.title: Canonical Signing Format:
docs.text:
The 64-byte Ed25519 signature is evaluated over the canonical byte concatenation:

SignBytes = UTF8(collection) + UTF8(id) + MutationTypeByte(0..2) + UTF8(hlcTimestamp) + payloadBytes

docs.title: AirDB Package Publishing & Distribution Guide
docs.text: This guide outlines the complete pipeline for publishing and distributing AirDB across the Android/JVM ecosystem (Maven Central / GitHub Packages) and the Apple ecosystem (Swift Package Manager / Swift Package Index).

docs.title: Step 1: Local Verification (publishToMavenLocal)

To verify POM generation, sources JARs, and javadoc JARs locally without publishing to external servers:

cd airdb
./gradlew publishToMavenLocal

This installs artifacts to your local cache at ~/.m2/repository/io/airdb/. You can inspect the generated .pom, -sources.jar, and .jar files.

docs.title: Step 2: Sonatype Central / Maven Central Preparation
docs.text:
Maven Central requires cryptographically signed artifacts (GPG) and valid POM metadata (license, developers, SCM):

  1. Create an account on Sonatype Central Portal.
  2. Claim Namespace: Verify ownership of io.airdb or io.github.untacorp via DNS TXT record or GitHub repository verification.
  3. Generate GPG Key: 
    gpg --gen-key
gpg --keyserver keyserver.ubuntu.com --send-keys <YOUR_KEY_ID>

    gpg --armor --export-secret-keys <YOUR_KEY_ID> | base64 -w 0

  6. MAVEN_CENTRAL_USERNAME: User token from Sonatype Central Portal.
  7. MAVEN_CENTRAL_PASSWORD: Password token from Sonatype Central Portal.
  8. SIGNING_KEY: Base64-encoded GPG private key.
  9. SIGNING_PASSWORD: Passphrase for the GPG key.

docs.title: Step 3: Publishing to Maven Central

Run the publish task:

./gradlew publishAllPublicationsToMavenCentralRepository

export GITHUB_ACTOR="untacorp"

./gradlew publishAllPublicationsToGitHubPackagesRepository

Any iOS, macOS, watchOS, or visionOS developer can add AirDB in Xcode: 1. Open Xcode, select File > Add Package Dependencies... 2. Enter repository URL: 

https://github.com/untacorp/airdb.git
3. Select version rule: Up to Next Major from 0.2.0.

docs.title: Creating a SemVer Release Tag

To create a new version release for both SPM and SPI:

# 1. Ensure working tree is clean and all tests pass
git status
./gradlew test
cd AirDbKit && swift test

# 2. Create git tag conforming to SemVer

docs.title: 4. Release Checklist

docs.title: Security Policy & Cryptographic Threat Model
docs.text: AirDB is designed from the ground up for hostile, disconnected, and untrusted peer-to-peer environments. This document outlines the cryptographic threat model, security guarantees, and vulnerability reporting procedures.

docs.title: 1. Supported Versions
docs.text:
Security updates are actively applied to the following versions of AirDB:

Version Supported 0.2.x Yes 0.1.x Yes

docs.title: 2. Threat Model & Security Guarantees
docs.text: In an off-grid BLE mesh network, communication occurs across an open RF broadcast channel and propagates through intermediate mobile devices acting as multi-hop gossip relays.

docs.title: Threat Vectors & Mitigations
docs.text: Threat Attack Vector AirDB Defense Mechanism Eavesdropping Passive RF sniffing of over-the-air BLE packets. ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD (256-bit symmetric cluster key). All payload data is ciphertext in flight. Packet Injection Rogue device broadcasts unauthorized frames into the cluster. Poly1305 16-byte MAC verification. Packets from unauthorized senders fail MAC checks and are dropped before parsing. Header Tampering Attacker modifies flags, timestamps, or recipient IDs in transit. Authenticated Additional Data (AAD). The entire 23B/31B header is cryptographically bound into the Poly1305 MAC. Malicious Mesh Relay Compromised intermediate peer alters record content or HLC timestamps. Ed25519 Asymmetric Signatures. Every mutation is signed by the originating author's private key. Intermediate relays cannot alter records without breaking the author's signature. Replay Attacks Attacker re-transmits valid past frames to roll back database state. Monotonic HLC & Vector Clock Filter. Replayed records with older or identical HLC timestamps are rejected by the LWW state machine. Buffer Overflow / DoS Malformed packet frames designed to crash JVM or Swift runtime. Defensive Wire Decoding. Strict bounds checking on magic bytes (0x41 0x44), payload lengths, Deflate decompressed buffer ceilings, and fragment reassembly timeouts (30s TTL).

docs.title: RFC 8439 ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD
docs.text:
• Android & Kotlin/JVM: Standard Java 17 Cryptographic Architecture (Cipher.getInstance("ChaCha20-Poly1305")).
  • Apple Platforms: Pure native Apple CryptoKit.ChaChaPoly.
  • Nonce Strategy: 12-byte cryptographically secure pseudo-random number generator (CSPRNG) generated per encrypted packet.
  • Tag Verification: 16-byte Poly1305 evaluation over AAD and ciphertext.

docs.title: RFC 8032 Ed25519 Digital Signatures
docs.text:
• Android & Kotlin/JVM: Java 17 Ed25519 via standard JCA KeyFactory and ASN.1 encoding bridges for raw 32-byte public keys and 32-byte private seed keys.
  • Apple Platforms: Pure native Apple CryptoKit.Curve25519.Signing.
  • Key Sizes: 32-byte public key, 64-byte signature.

docs.title: RFC 5869 HKDF-SHA256 Key Derivation
docs.text: • Uses HMAC-SHA256 extract-and-expand pipeline to derive 256-bit symmetric encryption keys from human-readable passwords, pre-shared cluster passphrases, or initial key material (IKM).

docs.title: 4. Reporting a Vulnerability
docs.text:
If you discover a security vulnerability within AirDB, please do not open a public GitHub issue. Send a responsible disclosure report to the maintainers at:

security@airdb.dev (or via private GitHub Security Advisory).

Please include: 1. Module and platform affected (JVM, Android, or Apple AirDbKit). 2. Steps or proof-of-concept code to reproduce the issue. 3. Potential impact of the vulnerability.

docs.title: ADR 0001: Sans-I/O Architecture for Core and Protocol
Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Mobile peer-to-peer applications frequently suffer from high testing friction, queue deadlocks, and flakey integration tests when network sockets or Bluetooth hardware APIs are interwoven directly into business logic. BitChat's V3 rewrite specifically highlighted the maintenance overhead of callback closures bridging queues into state.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: We decouple all state machines, causal clocks, data models, and binary protocol serializers completely from network and operating system I/O: 1. airdb-core, airdb-protocol, and airdb-adapter-api do not import any network or Android classes. 2. Inbound network data is ingested as raw byte arrays. 3. Outbound data is emitted as high-level packets or commands. 4. An in-memory virtual radio mesh simulator (airdb-transport-sim) is provided to test multi-node sync topologies without hardware.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Positive: 100% testable on pure JVM in milliseconds; 100% Kotlin Multiplatform (KMP) ready.
  • Negative: Requires clean interface boundaries (AirDbTransport, AirDbAdapter) between modules.

docs.title: ADR 0002: Hybrid Logical Clock (HLC) for Causality and Conflict Resolution
Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text: AirDB operates in partitioned, offline environments (disaster zones, outdoor markets) where devices have no access to NTP time servers. Device wall clocks can drift or be manually changed by users. Relying purely on physical timestamps leads to data loss or incorrect ordering.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
We implement a monotonic Hybrid Logical Clock (HLC) that tracks both physical epoch milliseconds and an incrementing logical counter. Each HLC timestamp also appends the unique node ID as a deterministic tie-breaker: physicalTime - logicalCounter - nodeId

Conflicts on identical record keys are resolved using Last-Write-Wins (LWW) based on total HLC ordering: HlcTimestampA > HlcTimestampB

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Positive: Strict causality preservation, monotonic progression even across clock resets, deterministic convergence without consensus rounds.
  • Negative: Last-Write-Wins operates at the record level; fine-grained column-level conflict resolution requires field-level CRDTs in future iterations.

docs.title: ADR 0003: Single-Flight GATT Queue for Android BLE
Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text: The Android Bluetooth stack (BlueDroid/Fluoride) allows only one outstanding GATT operation per connection. Firing simultaneous writes from background coroutines causes silent packet loss or GATT error codes (e.g. status 133 or GATT_BUSY).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: We introduce GattOperationQueue in airdb-transport-ble: 1. Every connection link owns a dedicated FIFO queue. 2. An inFlight state flag ensures that only the head operation is submitted to the OS. 3. The next operation is dispatched only when the driver invokes onCharacteristicWrite or onNotificationSent. 4. Transient errors are retried with exponential backoff before marking a link dead.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Positive: Complete elimination of race conditions and dropped packets on Android BLE.
  • Negative: Increases queuing latency slightly, bounded by BLE connection intervals (typically 7.5ms–15ms).

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text: AirDB was initially demonstrated with an in-memory database adapter (MemoryDbAdapter). For production deployments in disaster triage and mobile POS systems, nodes require durable disk persistence that survives application termination, power loss, and battery depletion. Furthermore, Apple platforms require a lightweight storage engine without bringing in heavy third-party SPM or CocoaPods dependencies (such as Realm, CoreData overhead, or third-party wrappers).

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: We introduce durable SQLite storage adapters conforming to AirDbAdapter: 1. JVM & Android: SqliteAirDbAdapter in :airdb-adapter-sqlite. 2. Apple Platforms: SqliteDbAdapter in AirDbKit utilizing native libsqlite3 C-bindings. 3. Database Engine Configuration: - Write-Ahead Logging enabled via PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL. - Synchronous disk writes set to PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL. - Foreign keys enabled where applicable. 4. Change Tracking & Tombstones: - A dedicated _airdb_changes table records mutation types (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE), HLC timestamps, author public keys, and signatures. - An index on hlc_timestamp ASC ensures range queries (getChangesSince) execute in \(\mathcal{O}(\log N + K)\) time. - Soft-delete tombstones prevent concurrent reconciliation from resurrecting deleted records.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Positive:
  • High write throughput and concurrent non-blocking reads via SQLite WAL.
  • Zero external package dependencies on Apple platforms.
  • Atomic transactions guarantee that delta batches are either applied in full or rolled back.
  • Negative:
  • Requires maintaining SQL schema evolution and tombstone compaction logic across two platforms.

docs.title: Status
docs.text: Accepted

docs.title: Context
docs.text: AirDB operates in ad-hoc, off-grid environments where nodes communicate via open Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) radio channels and multi-hop gossip topologies. This exposes data to three primary vulnerabilities: 1. Passive Eavesdropping: Third parties scanning 2.4 GHz RF channels can read plain-text survivor registries, medical notes, or commercial transactions. 2. Unauthorized Injection: Rogue devices within radio range can forge handshakes or inject corrupt database records. 3. Malicious Intermediate Relays: In a decentralized gossip mesh, intermediate devices forward packets. A compromised relay could alter record contents, swap IDs, or backdate HLC timestamps without detection.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text: We implement a two-layer Zero-Trust Cryptographic Mesh: 1. Cluster-Level Symmetric AEAD (RFC 8439 ChaCha20-Poly1305): - All packets between cluster members are encrypted with a 256-bit symmetric clusterKey. - Every packet generates a fresh 12-byte CSPRNG nonce. - The entire 23-byte (or 31-byte) wire header is passed as Authenticated Additional Data (\(AAD\)), binding version, packet type, flags, timestamp, and node IDs into the Poly1305 MAC tag. - Any packet with invalid MAC tag is discarded before parsing. 2. Record-Level Asymmetric Signatures (RFC 8032 Ed25519): - Each mutation is signed by its originating author using a private Ed25519 key. - The author's 32-byte public key and 64-byte signature are attached to the ChangeRecord. - The signature covers the canonical tuple: collection, id, mutationType, hlcTimestamp, and payload. - When enforceSignatures is active, receiving nodes verify the signature against the author public key. Compromised relays cannot tamper with records or timestamps without invalidating the cryptographic signature. 3. Key Derivation (RFC 5869 HKDF-SHA256): - Symmetric cluster keys and session materials are derived using HKDF-SHA256 with distinct domain separation tags. 4. Platform Native Implementations: - JVM & Android: Standard Java 17 JCA (ChaCha20-Poly1305 and Ed25519). - Apple Platforms: Pure native Apple CryptoKit (ChaChaPoly and Curve25519.Signing).

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Positive:
  • Full confidentiality against over-the-air RF sniffing.
  • Authentic framing prevents spoofed packet injections.
  • End-to-end cryptographic provenance protects against compromised or untrusted intermediate mesh relays.
  • Zero external third-party dependencies on both JVM and Apple platforms.
  • Negative:
  • Over-the-air packet overhead: 12-byte nonce + 16-byte Poly1305 tag per encrypted frame.
  • Record overhead: 32-byte public key + 64-byte signature per signed mutation.
  • Increased CPU consumption for cryptographic signature verification during large initial sync batches.

docs.title: Cookbook: Apple CoreData Integration (iOS & macOS)
docs.text: This guide shows how to integrate AirDB with CoreData in iOS and macOS applications using NSPersistentContainer and background execution contexts.

docs.title: 1. Managed Object Model Setup
docs.text:
In your .xcdatamodeld file, add an entity named AirDbChangeEntity:

Attribute Type Optional Indexed compositeKey String No Yes collection String No No recordId String No No mutationType Integer 16 No No payload Binary Data Yes No hlcTimestamp String No Yes authorPublicKey Binary Data Yes No signature Binary Data Yes No createdAt Date No No

docs.title: 2. Implementing AirDbAdapter
docs.text:
import AirDbKit
import CoreData
import Foundation

public final class CoreDataAirDbAdapter: AirDbAdapter, @unchecked Sendable {
    private let persistentContainer: NSPersistentContainer

    public init(persistentContainer: NSPersistentContainer) {
        self.persistentContainer = persistentContainer
    }

    public func getChangesSince(sinceHlcTimestamp: String?, limit: Int) async throws -> [ChangeRecord] {
        try await persistentContainer.performBackgroundTask { context in
            let request = NSFetchRequest<NSManagedObject>(entityName: "AirDbChangeEntity")

            if let since = sinceHlcTimestamp {
                request.predicate = NSPredicate(format: "hlcTimestamp > %@", since)
            }
            request.sortDescriptors = [NSSortDescriptor(key: "hlcTimestamp", ascending: true)]
            request.fetchLimit = limit

            let results = try context.fetch(request)
            return results.compactMap { obj -> ChangeRecord? in
                guard let id = obj.value(forKey: "recordId") as? String,
                      let collection = obj.value(forKey: "collection") as? String,
                      let rawType = obj.value(forKey: "mutationType") as? Int16,
                      let type = MutationType(rawValue: Int(rawType)),
                      let hlc = obj.value(forKey: "hlcTimestamp") as? String else {
                    return nil
                }

                let payload = obj.value(forKey: "payload") as? Data ?? Data()
                let authorPublicKey = obj.value(forKey: "authorPublicKey") as? Data
                let signature = obj.value(forKey: "signature") as? Data

                return ChangeRecord(
                    id: id,
                    collection: collection,
                    type: type,
                    payload: payload,
                    hlcTimestamp: hlc,
                    authorPublicKey: authorPublicKey,
                    signature: signature
                )
            }
        }
    }

    public func applyChanges(_ changes: [ChangeRecord]) async throws {
        try await persistentContainer.performBackgroundTask { context in
            for change in changes {
                let targetKey = "\(change.collection):\(change.id)"
                let request = NSFetchRequest<NSManagedObject>(entityName: "AirDbChangeEntity")
                request.predicate = NSPredicate(format: "compositeKey == %@", targetKey)
                request.fetchLimit = 1

                let existing = try context.fetch(request).first
                let currentHlc = existing?.value(forKey: "hlcTimestamp") as? String

                // Last-Write-Wins (LWW) check
                if currentHlc == nil || change.hlcTimestamp > currentHlc! {
                    let obj = existing ?? NSEntityDescription.insertNewObject(
                        forEntityName: "AirDbChangeEntity",
                        into: context
                    )

                    obj.setValue(targetKey, forKey: "compositeKey")
                    obj.setValue(change.collection, forKey: "collection")
                    obj.setValue(change.id, forKey: "recordId")
                    obj.setValue(Int16(change.type.rawValue), forKey: "mutationType")
                    obj.setValue(change.payload, forKey: "payload")
                    obj.setValue(change.hlcTimestamp, forKey: "hlcTimestamp")
                    obj.setValue(change.authorPublicKey, forKey: "authorPublicKey")
                    obj.setValue(change.signature, forKey: "signature")
                    obj.setValue(Date(), forKey: "createdAt")
                }
            }

            if context.hasChanges {
                try context.save()
            }
        }
    }

    public func getLatestHlc() async throws -> String? {
        try await persistentContainer.performBackgroundTask { context in
            let request = NSFetchRequest<NSManagedObject>(entityName: "AirDbChangeEntity")
            request.sortDescriptors = [NSSortDescriptor(key: "hlcTimestamp", ascending: false)]
            request.fetchLimit = 1
            let result = try context.fetch(request).first
            return result?.value(forKey: "hlcTimestamp") as? String
        }
    }
}

docs.title: Cookbook: GRDB.swift Integration (iOS & macOS)
docs.text: GRDB.swift is a toolkit for SQLite databases in Swift applications. This guide shows how to implement AirDbAdapter with GRDB using DatabaseQueue or DatabasePool.

docs.title: 1. Schema Migration (AirDbMigration)
docs.text:
Define the changelog table in your GRDB DatabaseMigrator:

import GRDB

extension DatabaseMigrator {
    mutating func registerAirDbMigrations() {
        registerMigration("createAirDbChangelog") { db in
            try db.create(table: "_airdb_changes") { t in
                t.column("collection", .text).notNull()
                t.column("id", .text).notNull()
                t.column("mutation_type", .integer).notNull()
                t.column("payload", .blob)
                t.column("hlc_timestamp", .text).notNull()
                t.column("author_public_key", .blob)
                t.column("signature", .blob)
                t.column("created_at", .integer).notNull()

                t.primaryKey(["collection", "id"])
            }

            try db.create(
                index: "idx_airdb_changes_hlc",
                on: "_airdb_changes",
                columns: ["hlc_timestamp"]
            )
        }
    }
}

docs.title: 2. Implementing AirDbAdapter
docs.text:
import AirDbKit
import Foundation
import GRDB

public final class GrdbAirDbAdapter: AirDbAdapter, @unchecked Sendable {
    private let dbWriter: any DatabaseWriter

    public init(dbWriter: any DatabaseWriter) {
        self.dbWriter = dbWriter
    }

    public func getChangesSince(sinceHlcTimestamp: String?, limit: Int) async throws -> [ChangeRecord] {
        try await dbWriter.read { db in
            let sql: String
            let arguments: StatementArguments

            if let since = sinceHlcTimestamp {
                sql = "SELECT * FROM _airdb_changes WHERE hlc_timestamp > ? ORDER BY hlc_timestamp ASC LIMIT ?"
                arguments = [since, limit]
            } else {
                sql = "SELECT * FROM _airdb_changes ORDER BY hlc_timestamp ASC LIMIT ?"
                arguments = [limit]
            }

            let rows = try Row.fetchAll(db, sql: sql, arguments: arguments)
            return rows.compactMap { row -> ChangeRecord? in
                guard let id: String = row["id"],
                      let collection: String = row["collection"],
                      let rawType: Int = row["mutation_type"],
                      let type = MutationType(rawValue: rawType),
                      let hlc: String = row["hlc_timestamp"] else {
                    return nil
                }

                let payload: Data = row["payload"] ?? Data()
                let authorPublicKey: Data? = row["author_public_key"]
                let signature: Data? = row["signature"]

                return ChangeRecord(
                    id: id,
                    collection: collection,
                    type: type,
                    payload: payload,
                    hlcTimestamp: hlc,
                    authorPublicKey: authorPublicKey,
                    signature: signature
                )
            }
        }
    }

    public func applyChanges(_ changes: [ChangeRecord]) async throws {
        try await dbWriter.write { db in
            let now = Int64(Date().timeIntervalSince1970 * 1000)

            for change in changes {
                let currentHlc = try String.fetchOne(
                    db,
                    sql: "SELECT hlc_timestamp FROM _airdb_changes WHERE collection = ? AND id = ?",
                    arguments: [change.collection, change.id]
                )

                // Last-Write-Wins (LWW) check
                if currentHlc == nil || change.hlcTimestamp > currentHlc! {
                    try db.execute(
                        sql: """
                        INSERT OR REPLACE INTO _airdb_changes (
                            collection, id, mutation_type, payload, hlc_timestamp, author_public_key, signature, created_at
                        ) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)
                        """,
                        arguments: [
                            change.collection,
                            change.id,
                            change.type.rawValue,
                            change.payload,
                            change.hlcTimestamp,
                            change.authorPublicKey,
                            change.signature,
                            now
                        ]
                    )
                }
            }
        }
    }

    public func getLatestHlc() async throws -> String? {
        try await dbWriter.read { db in
            try String.fetchOne(db, sql: "SELECT MAX(hlc_timestamp) FROM _airdb_changes")
        }
    }
}

docs.title: 2. Custom Key-Value Store Implementation
docs.text:
If you want to back AirDB with an existing in-memory cache (such as Caffeine, an LRU cache, or Redis):

package com.example.cache

import io.airdb.adapter.AirDbAdapter
import io.airdb.adapter.ChangeRecord
import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentHashMap
import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentSkipListMap

class CustomMemoryKvAdapter : AirDbAdapter {

    // Primary record storage: (collection:id) -> ChangeRecord
    private val records = ConcurrentHashMap<String, ChangeRecord>()

    // HLC-ordered index: hlcTimestamp -> (collection:id)
    private val hlcIndex = ConcurrentSkipListMap<String, String>()

    override suspend fun getChangesSince(sinceHlcTimestamp: String?, limit: Int): List<ChangeRecord> {
        val tailMap = if (sinceHlcTimestamp == null) {
            hlcIndex
        } else {
            hlcIndex.tailMap(sinceHlcTimestamp, false)
        }

        return tailMap.values
            .take(limit)
            .mapNotNull { key -> records[key] }
    }

    override suspend fun applyChanges(changes: List<ChangeRecord>) {
        for (change in changes) {
            val key = "${change.collection}:${change.id}"
            records.compute(key) { _, existing ->
                if (existing == null || change.hlcTimestamp > existing.hlcTimestamp) {
                    if (existing != null) {
                        hlcIndex.remove(existing.hlcTimestamp)
                    }
                    hlcIndex[change.hlcTimestamp] = key
                    change
                } else {
                    existing
                }
            }
        }
    }

    override suspend fun getLatestHlc(): String? {
        return hlcIndex.lastKey()
    }
}

docs.title: Cookbook: Android Jetpack Room Integration
docs.text: This guide demonstrates how to integrate AirDB into an Android application that uses Android Jetpack Room for local persistence.

docs.title: 1. Schema Definition (Room Entities)
docs.text:
Add a changelog entity to your Room schema alongside your domain tables:

package com.example.app.data.local

import androidx.room.Entity
import androidx.room.Index
import androidx.room.PrimaryKey

@Entity(
    tableName = "airdb_changelog",
    indices = [
        Index(value = ["hlcTimestamp"], unique = false),
        Index(value = ["collection", "recordId"], unique = false)
    ]
)
data class ChangelogEntity(
    @PrimaryKey(autoGenerate = true)
    val localId: Long = 0,
    val collection: String,
    val recordId: String,
    val mutationType: String, // INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE
    val payload: ByteArray,
    val hlcTimestamp: String,
    val authorPublicKey: ByteArray? = null,
    val signature: ByteArray? = null,
    val createdAt: Long = System.currentTimeMillis()
)

And your domain entity (for example, emergency disaster survivors):

@Entity(tableName = "survivors")
data class SurvivorEntity(
    @PrimaryKey
    val id: String,
    val name: String,
    val triageStatus: String, // RED, YELLOW, GREEN, BLACK
    val location: String,
    val updatedAtHlc: String
)

docs.title: 2. Room DAO Definition
docs.text:
package com.example.app.data.local

import androidx.room.Dao
import androidx.room.Insert
import androidx.room.OnConflictStrategy
import androidx.room.Query
import androidx.room.Transaction

@Dao
interface AirDbDao {

    @Query("SELECT * FROM airdb_changelog WHERE hlcTimestamp > :sinceHlc ORDER BY hlcTimestamp ASC LIMIT :limit")
    suspend fun getChangesAfter(sinceHlc: String, limit: Int): List<ChangelogEntity>

    @Query("SELECT * FROM airdb_changelog ORDER BY hlcTimestamp ASC LIMIT :limit")
    suspend fun getEarliestChanges(limit: Int): List<ChangelogEntity>

    @Query("SELECT MAX(hlcTimestamp) FROM airdb_changelog")
    suspend fun getMaxHlc(): String?

    @Query("SELECT hlcTimestamp FROM airdb_changelog WHERE collection = :collection AND recordId = :recordId ORDER BY hlcTimestamp DESC LIMIT 1")
    suspend fun getLatestHlcForRecord(collection: String, recordId: String): String?

    @Insert(onConflict = OnConflictStrategy.REPLACE)
    suspend fun insertChangelog(entry: ChangelogEntity)

    // Domain queries
    @Insert(onConflict = OnConflictStrategy.REPLACE)
    suspend fun upsertSurvivor(survivor: SurvivorEntity)

    @Query("DELETE FROM survivors WHERE id = :id")
    suspend fun deleteSurvivor(id: String)
}

docs.title: 3. Implementing AirDbAdapter
docs.text:
package com.example.app.data.local

import androidx.room.withTransaction
import io.airdb.adapter.AirDbAdapter
import io.airdb.adapter.ChangeRecord
import io.airdb.adapter.MutationType
import org.json.JSONObject

class RoomAirDbAdapter(
    private val database: AppDatabase
) : AirDbAdapter {

    private val dao = database.airDbDao()

    override suspend fun getChangesSince(sinceHlcTimestamp: String?, limit: Int): List<ChangeRecord> {
        val rows = if (sinceHlcTimestamp == null) {
            dao.getEarliestChanges(limit)
        } else {
            dao.getChangesAfter(sinceHlcTimestamp, limit)
        }

        return rows.map { row ->
            ChangeRecord(
                id = row.recordId,
                collection = row.collection,
                type = MutationType.valueOf(row.mutationType),
                payload = row.payload,
                hlcTimestamp = row.hlcTimestamp,
                authorPublicKey = row.authorPublicKey,
                signature = row.signature
            )
        }
    }

    override suspend fun applyChanges(changes: List<ChangeRecord>) {
        database.withTransaction {
            for (change in changes) {
                val currentHlc = dao.getLatestHlcForRecord(change.collection, change.id)

                // Last-Write-Wins (LWW) check: only apply if change is strictly newer
                if (currentHlc == null || change.hlcTimestamp > currentHlc) {
                    // 1. Record to sync changelog
                    dao.insertChangelog(
                        ChangelogEntity(
                            collection = change.collection,
                            recordId = change.id,
                            mutationType = change.type.name,
                            payload = change.payload,
                            hlcTimestamp = change.hlcTimestamp,
                            authorPublicKey = change.authorPublicKey,
                            signature = change.signature
                        )
                    )

                    // 2. Project into domain tables
                    if (change.collection == "survivors") {
                        when (change.type) {
                            MutationType.INSERT, MutationType.UPDATE -> {
                                val json = JSONObject(String(change.payload, Charsets.UTF_8))
                                val entity = SurvivorEntity(
                                    id = change.id,
                                    name = json.getString("name"),
                                    triageStatus = json.getString("triageStatus"),
                                    location = json.getString("location"),
                                    updatedAtHlc = change.hlcTimestamp
                                )
                                dao.upsertSurvivor(entity)
                            }
                            MutationType.DELETE -> {
                                dao.deleteSurvivor(change.id)
                            }
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    override suspend fun getLatestHlc(): String? {
        return dao.getMaxHlc()
    }
}

docs.title: Cookbook: SQLDelight Multiplatform Integration
docs.text: This guide demonstrates how to integrate AirDB with SQLDelight (Kotlin Multiplatform / Android / JVM / iOS).

docs.title: 1. Schema Definition (AirDbChangelog.sq)
docs.text:
Create an SQLDelight definition file in src/commonMain/sqldelight/io/airdb/storage/AirDbChangelog.sq:

    collection TEXT NOT NULL,
    id TEXT NOT NULL,
    mutation_type INTEGER NOT NULL,
    payload BLOB NOT NULL,
    hlc_timestamp TEXT NOT NULL,
    author_public_key BLOB,
    signature BLOB,
    created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (collection, id)
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_airdb_changelog_hlc
ON airdb_changelog(hlc_timestamp ASC);

-- Queries:

WHERE hlc_timestamp > :sinceHlc
ORDER BY hlc_timestamp ASC
LIMIT :limit;

getEarliestChanges:

ORDER BY hlc_timestamp ASC
LIMIT :limit;
