docs.title: 2. Implementing AirDbAdapter
docs.text:
package io.airdb.storage.sqldelight

import io.airdb.adapter.AirDbAdapter
import io.airdb.adapter.ChangeRecord
import io.airdb.adapter.MutationType
import io.airdb.storage.AirDbDatabase

class SqlDelightAirDbAdapter(
    private val database: AirDbDatabase
) : AirDbAdapter {

    private val queries = database.airDbChangelogQueries

    override suspend fun getChangesSince(sinceHlcTimestamp: String?, limit: Int): List<ChangeRecord> {
        val rows = if (sinceHlcTimestamp == null) {
            queries.getEarliestChanges(limit.toLong()).executeAsList()
        } else {
            queries.getChangesAfter(sinceHlcTimestamp, limit.toLong()).executeAsList()
        }

        return rows.map { row ->
            ChangeRecord(
                id = row.id,
                collection = row.collection,
                type = MutationType.entries[row.mutation_type.toInt()],
                payload = row.payload,
                hlcTimestamp = row.hlc_timestamp,
                authorPublicKey = row.author_public_key,
                signature = row.signature
            )
        }
    }

    override suspend fun applyChanges(changes: List<ChangeRecord>) {
        database.transaction {
            val now = System.currentTimeMillis()
            for (change in changes) {
                val currentHlc = queries.getRecordHlc(change.collection, change.id).executeAsOneOrNull()

                // Last-Write-Wins (LWW) check
                if (currentHlc == null || change.hlcTimestamp > currentHlc) {
                    queries.upsertChange(
                        collection = change.collection,
                        id = change.id,
                        mutationType = change.type.ordinal.toLong(),
                        payload = change.payload,
                        hlcTimestamp = change.hlcTimestamp,
                        authorPublicKey = change.authorPublicKey,
                        signature = change.signature,
                        createdAt = now
                    )
                }
            }
        }
    }

    override suspend fun getLatestHlc(): String? {
        return queries.getLatestHlc().executeAsOneOrNull()?.MAX
    }
}

docs.title: Cookbook: Native SQLite Adapter for Android & JVM
docs.text: AirDB includes an optimized, production-ready SQLite persistence engine in the :airdb-adapter-sqlite module. It features automatic schema management, Write-Ahead Logging (WAL mode), monotonic HLC indexing, and tombstone lifecycle handling.

docs.title: 1. Dependency Setup
docs.text:
Add :airdb-adapter-sqlite to your application's build.gradle.kts:

dependencies {
    implementation("io.airdb:airdb-core:0.2.0")
    implementation("io.airdb:airdb-adapter-sqlite:0.2.0")
    implementation("io.airdb:airdb-transport-ble:0.2.0")
}

docs.title: 2. Basic Initialization
docs.text:
import io.airdb.adapter.sqlite.SqliteAirDbAdapter
import java.io.File

// For Android applications:
val dbPath = context.getDatabasePath("airdb_local.db").absolutePath

// For JVM server / CLI applications:
// val dbPath = File("./data/airdb_local.db").absolutePath

val adapter = SqliteAirDbAdapter(dbPath = dbPath)

The adapter automatically executes: - PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL; (enables concurrent readers during writes) - PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL; (optimal balance of performance and crash durability) - Creates _airdb_changes table and idx_airdb_changes_hlc index if they do not exist.

docs.title: 3. Direct Domain Integration & Mutation Recording
docs.text:
To record changes in your local database and propagate them across the BLE mesh:

import io.airdb.adapter.MutationType

// 1. Create your AirDB engine with the SQLite adapter
val engine = AirDbEngine(
    nodeName = "posko-merapi-01",
    adapter = adapter,
    transport = transport,
    clusterKey = clusterKey,
    authorKeyPair = authorKeyPair,
    enforceSignatures = true
)

// 2. Start synchronization
engine.start()

// 3. Save a record locally
val jsonPayload = """
{
    "itemId": "MED-501",
    "name": "Antibiotics Amoxicillin 500mg",
    "quantity": 250,
    "unit": "box"
}
""".trimIndent().toByteArray(Charsets.UTF_8)

val changeRecord = engine.saveRecord(
    collection = "medical_supplies",
    id = "MED-501",
    type = MutationType.INSERT,
    payload = jsonPayload
)

println("Saved record ${changeRecord.id} with HLC ${changeRecord.hlcTimestamp}")

docs.title: 4. Observing Changes with Sync Listeners
docs.text:
Listen for mutations arriving from nearby peers over Bluetooth:

engine.addSyncListener { peerId, changeCount ->
    println("Received and applied $changeCount mutations from peer: $peerId")

    // Query the latest state from your UI / state flow
    // ...
}

docs.title: Cookbook: Built-in Native SQLite Adapter for Apple Platforms
docs.text: AirDbKit includes an out-of-the-box durable persistence engine: SqliteDbAdapter. It is implemented directly on top of Apple's system libsqlite3 C library, which means zero third-party dependencies (no GRDB, no SQLite.swift, and no external CocoaPods/SPM packages).

docs.title: 1. Key Features
docs.text:
• Zero External Dependencies: Uses native Apple system import SQLite3.
  • Write-Ahead Logging (WAL mode): Supports concurrent non-blocking reads while writing mutations.
  • Indexed HLC Range Queries: Fast \(\mathcal{O}(\log N + K)\) delta fetches via idx_airdb_changes_hlc.
  • Atomic Transactions: Batch changes are wrapped in immediate transactions (BEGIN IMMEDIATE ... COMMIT).
  • Thread Safety: Fully thread-safe across Swift concurrency tasks using scoped locks (NSLock.withScopedLock).

docs.title: 2. Basic Usage
docs.text:
import AirDbKit
import Foundation

// 1. Locate documents directory
let fileManager = FileManager.default
let documentsUrl = fileManager.urls(for: .documentDirectory, in: .userDomainMask)[0]
let databasePath = documentsUrl.appendingPathComponent("airdb_production.db").path

// 2. Initialize SqliteDbAdapter
let adapter = try SqliteDbAdapter(databasePath: databasePath)

// 3. Initialize BLE Transport
let transport = CoreBluetoothTransport()

// 4. Start AirDB Engine
let engine = AirDbEngine(
    nodeName: "posko-field-ipad-01",
    adapter = adapter,
    transport = transport,
    clusterKey = clusterKey,
    authorKeyPair = authorKeyPair,
    enforceSignatures = true
)

engine.start()

docs.title: 3. Saving & Reading Records
docs.text:
// Record an insert or update
let jsonString = """
{
    "patientId": "SURVIVOR-204",
    "name": "Agus Santoso",
    "status": "Evacuated to Base Hospital",
    "triage": "GREEN"
}
"""
let payloadData = jsonString.data(using: .utf8)!

let record = try await engine.saveRecord(
    collection: "triage_registry",
    id: "SURVIVOR-204",
    type: .insert,
    payload: payloadData
)

print("Saved record with HLC: \(record.hlcTimestamp)")

docs.title: 4. Deleting Records (Tombstone Propagation)
docs.text:
AirDB treats deletions as first-class mutations. To delete a record:

try await engine.saveRecord(
    collection: "triage_registry",
    id: "SURVIVOR-204",
    type: .delete,
    payload: Data() // empty payload for tombstones
)

The tombstone will be assigned a new HLC timestamp and automatically propagated to nearby devices, ensuring all replicas delete the record and prevent older writes from resurrecting it.

docs.title: Cookbook: Apple SwiftData Integration (iOS 17+ & macOS 14+)
docs.text: This guide shows how to integrate AirDB with SwiftData, Apple's modern persistence framework using @Model and ModelContainer.

docs.title: 1. Defining the @Model Changelog Entity
docs.text:
import Foundation
import SwiftData

@Model
public final class AirDbChangeEntity {
    @Attribute(.unique)
    public var compositeKey: String // collection + ":" + id

    public var collection: String
    public var recordId: String
    public var mutationType: Int
    public var payload: Data

    #Index([\.hlcTimestamp])
    public var hlcTimestamp: String

    public var authorPublicKey: Data?
    public var signature: Data?
    public var createdAt: Date

    public init(
        collection: String,
        recordId: String,
        mutationType: Int,
        payload: Data,
        hlcTimestamp: String,
        authorPublicKey: Data? = nil,
        signature: Data? = nil,
        createdAt: Date = Date()
    ) {
        self.compositeKey = "\(collection):\(recordId)"
        self.collection = collection
        self.recordId = recordId
        self.mutationType = mutationType
        self.payload = payload
        self.hlcTimestamp = hlcTimestamp
        self.authorPublicKey = authorPublicKey
        self.signature = signature
        self.createdAt = createdAt
    }
}

docs.title: 2. Implementing AirDbAdapter with a Background ModelContext
docs.text:
Because SwiftData's ModelContext is bound to specific actors/threads, use ModelContainer.newContext() or a dedicated background actor:

import AirDbKit
import Foundation
import SwiftData

@ModelActor
public actor SwiftDataAirDbAdapter: AirDbAdapter {

    public func getChangesSince(sinceHlcTimestamp: String?, limit: Int) throws -> [ChangeRecord] {
        var descriptor: FetchDescriptor<AirDbChangeEntity>

        if let since = sinceHlcTimestamp {
            descriptor = FetchDescriptor<AirDbChangeEntity>(
                predicate: #Predicate { $0.hlcTimestamp > since },
                sortBy: [SortDescriptor(\.hlcTimestamp, order: .forward)]
            )
        } else {
            descriptor = FetchDescriptor<AirDbChangeEntity>(
                sortBy: [SortDescriptor(\.hlcTimestamp, order: .forward)]
            )
        }

        descriptor.fetchLimit = limit
        let entities = try modelContext.fetch(descriptor)

        return entities.compactMap { entity in
            guard let type = MutationType(rawValue: entity.mutationType) else { return nil }
            return ChangeRecord(
                id: entity.recordId,
                collection: entity.collection,
                type: type,
                payload: entity.payload,
                hlcTimestamp: entity.hlcTimestamp,
                authorPublicKey: entity.authorPublicKey,
                signature: entity.signature
            )
        }
    }

    public func applyChanges(_ changes: [ChangeRecord]) throws {
        for change in changes {
            let targetKey = "\(change.collection):\(change.id)"
            var descriptor = FetchDescriptor<AirDbChangeEntity>(
                predicate: #Predicate { $0.compositeKey == targetKey }
            )
            descriptor.fetchLimit = 1

            let existing = try modelContext.fetch(descriptor).first

            // Last-Write-Wins (LWW) check
            if existing == nil || change.hlcTimestamp > existing!.hlcTimestamp {
                if let existing = existing {
                    existing.mutationType = change.type.rawValue
                    existing.payload = change.payload
                    existing.hlcTimestamp = change.hlcTimestamp
                    existing.authorPublicKey = change.authorPublicKey
                    existing.signature = change.signature
                    existing.createdAt = Date()
                } else {
                    let newEntity = AirDbChangeEntity(
                        collection: change.collection,
                        recordId: change.id,
                        mutationType: change.type.rawValue,
                        payload: change.payload,
                        hlcTimestamp: change.hlcTimestamp,
                        authorPublicKey: change.authorPublicKey,
                        signature: change.signature
                    )
                    modelContext.insert(newEntity)
                }
            }
        }

        try modelContext.save()
    }

    public func getLatestHlc() throws -> String? {
        var descriptor = FetchDescriptor<AirDbChangeEntity>(
            sortBy: [SortDescriptor(\.hlcTimestamp, order: .reverse)]
        )
        descriptor.fetchLimit = 1
        return try modelContext.fetch(descriptor).first?.hlcTimestamp
    }
}

docs.title: 3. Initialization in SwiftUI / iOS Application
docs.text:
import AirDbKit
import SwiftData
import SwiftUI

@main
struct PoskoApp: App {
    let container: ModelContainer
    let adapter: SwiftDataAirDbAdapter
    let engine: AirDbEngine

    init() {
        do {
            let schema = Schema([AirDbChangeEntity.self, SurvivorModel.self])
            container = try ModelContainer(for: schema)
            adapter = SwiftDataAirDbAdapter(modelContainer: container)

            let transport = CoreBluetoothTransport()
            engine = AirDbEngine(
                nodeName: "ios-responder-device",
                adapter: adapter,
                transport = transport
            )
            engine.start()
        } catch {
            fatalError("Failed to initialize database container: \(error)")
        }
    }

    var body: some Scene {
        WindowGroup {
            ContentView()
        }
        .modelContainer(container)
    }
}
